chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Ibn Abi Umeyr from one of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds, so We shall render them as scattered floating dust.' He said: 'Even if their deeds were intensely whiter than the tapestries, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would say to them: Be scattered floating dust!' And that is because whenever the prohibited [means] was displayed unto them, they grabbed it.
ai.seo_question: Why are deeds nullified even if they appear righteous?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the nullification of deeds due to haram earnings is not merely a loss of reward but a total erasure of the deed's essence, reducing even the brightest actions to 'scattered dust' (haba' manthoor). This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the source of sustenance acts as a foundational determinant for the validity of worship, where consuming the prohibited corrupts the spiritual integrity of all other acts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, form Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [25:23] And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds, so We shall render them as scattered floating dust. So heasws said: ‘Even if their deeds were intensely whiter than the tapestries, so Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would be Saying to these: “Be floating dust!”, and that is because whenever the Prohibited means was displayed unto them, they grabbed it’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘We arrived upon what they had done and turned it into scattered dust’, [25:25] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’
Even if their deeds are whiter than Coptic fabrics Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “Become dust.” It is because when they come upon unlawful matters they take it.’”
